explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Luke 8:19 says Jesus' mother and brothers came to see Him. Family showed up, and a whole crowd was standing between them and Him. I know that feeling. Ever try to get to the front of a line when everybody's already in it?

Martha and Mary are real people in Luke, friend. They're sisters, and Luke 10:38 says Martha welcomed Jesus into her home. But they aren't the visitors here. Luke 8:19 says it's Jesus' mother and brothers who came. Easy mix-up, since Luke has so many people showing up at once.

Peter and Andrew, the fishermen brothers, were part of Jesus' followers (Matthew 4:18-20). Good guess with the brothers part. But Luke 8:19 says the ones who came to see Him were His mother and brothers. Brothers, yes. Just a different set.

Oh, I wish it were that smooth, baker. Luke 8:19 says they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd. So nobody walked right up. They were stuck out there, and the crowd had the whole front of the line.
Right, friend. Luke 8:19 says they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd. No walking up to Him. Then Luke 8:20 says He was told they were there, and that's what happens next.

You got it, baker. Someone tells Jesus, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You." (Luke 8:20) They're standing right there, just on the wrong side of that crowd. I think that has to feel rough, standing out there while a whole crowd stays put.

Upstairs is a fun guess, friend, but that's not the word. Luke 8:20 says they are standing outside, wanting to see Him. The text gives us that one word, so I'll stick with outside. Nothing in the story points upstairs.

Close, baker, but it's the opposite word. Luke 8:20 says His mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see Him. Luke 8:19 says the crowd kept them from reaching Him. So outside is the word that fits.

explanations.answer: Those who hear God's word and carry it out
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Jesus says, "My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out." (Luke 8:21) Two things go together there: hearing and doing. It's like a recipe, friend. Reading it won't give you a single cookie until you actually turn on the oven.

explanations.answer: Those who follow Him from town to town
explanations.explanation: Luke does mention people traveling with Jesus from town to town (Luke 8:1). But that isn't what He says here, friend. In Luke 8:21 He says His mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out. It's about hearing and doing, not about where somebody walks.

explanations.answer: Those who sit closest to Him and listen
explanations.explanation: Sitting close sounds right, baker. But Jesus doesn't talk about who sits where. He says, "My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out." (Luke 8:21) Listening is only half of it. The doing is the other half.
